subject: Food Science
title: Hand Hygiene
description: A quick, practical guide to Hand Hygiene.

hook.text: Fifty percent of foodborne outbreaks from restaurants trace back to food handler hygiene. Dirty hands are the main vector.

buildup.text: Proper hand washing means 20 seconds with warm water and soap—scrubbing palms, backs, fingers, nails, and wrists.

discovery.text: The average person touches their face 23 times per hour. Each touch transfers microbes from surfaces to mucous membranes.

twist.text: Gloves give a false sense of security. Workers wearing gloves change them less frequently than they would wash bare hands.

climax.text: Hand washing after using the toilet reduces bacterial counts by 99%. After handling raw meat, by 99.5%. The math is clear.

punchline.text: Twenty seconds of soap stops 99% of transfer. The simplest tool in food safety.

quiz.question: Why can gloves be a food safety risk?
options: Workers change gloves less frequently than they would wash bare hands
